decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approaches: left toward the left watch, right toward the right toy car. Raise and gradually pitch grippers downward before descending.
Continue small elbow-up increments toward overhead grasps on the left watch and right car; keep both grippers open.
Fine-align from wrist views, finish downward orientation and close on watch/car. Retention remains to be checked during lift.
Lift vertically with both grippers fully closed to verify whether watch and car are retained before moving toward baskets.
Neither object followed the lift. Reopen and shift forward from wrist-image offsets, then descend for a better-centered grasp.
Close around the recentered watch and test a small lift. Align the right gripper across the car's diagonal width before closing.
Test car retention with a vertical lift. The hollow watch was not retained; aim at its solid right-hand face/band instead, lower slightly and close.
Car appears retained; carry it above the center blue basket without crossing arms. Lift the watch grasp vertically to inspect retention.

Replan after the IK guard: smaller rightward-basket approach increments with forward tilt to preserve elbow-up reach. Retry the watch lower and nearer its observed center, keeping it open during positioning.
Close on the now-centered watch and check a short vertical lift. The car slipped onto the table; reopen the right gripper and approach its new position with a downward grip across its width.
Watch follows the left gripper; carry it toward the white basket with gentle orientation change. Fine-position the open right gripper over the fallen car using the wrist view.
Advance the retained watch fully inside the white basket and release. Close around the recentered car and perform a slow short lift without changing orientation.
Watch is released in white. Withdraw the left arm toward the remaining watch; slowly move the retained car over the right half of blue, preserving elbow-up continuity.
The car has slipped off-center, so reopen and recenter rather than assuming retention. Approach the second watch with the left gripper, remaining on the left side.
Use wrist offsets to center the remaining watch and fallen car. Lower open grippers for deeper grasps; the right car is visibly on the table now.
Replan from the interrupted poses. Move the right arm outward to clear the closely spaced grippers; finish the left watch grasp and test a short lift.
Lift the second watch before carrying leftward. With the arms separating, bring the right open gripper back toward the fallen car using smaller wrist-guided corrections.
Carry the visibly retained second watch toward white at rim clearance. Recenter the right gripper across the car, descend slightly, and close without changing its orientation.
Place and release the second watch inside white, alongside the first. Keep the right grip closed and lift the car slowly to check whether it remains centered.
Both watches are in white. Approach the two cars with open grippers, rotating the jaws across each car's shorter width; the right car did not remain held.
Lower open grippers toward the two cars, finish widthwise jaw alignment, and remove the right wrist's residual tilt before a deeper grasp.
Correct visible wrist offsets: left car is right/forward of the jaw center; right car is forward. Recenter before closing both widthwise grips.
Both cars are now between widthwise jaws. Hold closed and make slow vertical test lifts, without wrist rotation or lateral motion.
Both cars followed the lifts. Carry them toward opposite halves of blue with added rim clearance, slow translation and only a small forward pitch; maintain closed grips.
Replan after right IK rejection: avoid further forward EE extension. Gradually pitch the held cars toward blue while making only small position adjustments.
Separate the grippers after left tracking resistance. Hold the left car aside while moving the right car fully over blue and opening to release it.
Right car is released over blue; withdraw right to clear the center. The left car slipped beside the front rim, so reopen and realign the jaws across its new width for another grasp.
Recenter left over the car's new location beside white/blue. Approach the rightmost white pen with the right arm, orienting the open jaws across the pen.
Close a centered left grasp on the car's solid body. Bring the right wrist to a vertical, low pen grasp using the visible pen center rather than the link position.
Lift the centered car vertically with no wrist change. The pen is offset across the right jaws and the previous descent met the table; reopen, lift slightly and correct laterally before reclosing.
The left car followed its vertical lift; carry it gradually toward blue while keeping rim clearance. Test the white pen grasp with a straight right-arm lift.
Move the retained car into the left half of blue before releasing. The right pen fell; reopen and realign the jaw direction across its new diagonal orientation.
Reduce left height and use a small inward wrist tilt rather than extending farther after the IK rejection. Recenter the open right gripper over the fallen pen while completing widthwise alignment.
Release the second car inside blue and withdraw the left gripper. Lower the right gripper carefully onto the aligned white pen and close across its shaft.
Both cars are now inside blue. Approach the black pen with the left gripper aligned across its shaft, while testing right white-pen retention with a slow vertical lift.
White pen appears retained; carry it gradually toward red without changing the grip. Lower and close the left jaws across the black pen after a small alignment correction.
Lift the black pen and orient it for staging near the center for a later right-arm pickup, without crossing arms. Continue carrying the retained white pen toward red.
Release the white pen inside red. Lay the black pen horizontally across the center staging area with its right end accessible, then open the left gripper for a non-crossing transfer.
Keep both grippers open while clearing the released pens. Withdraw the left arm, and approach the remaining white pen with the right jaws turned across its shaft.
Return the empty left arm toward origin with continuous elbow-up motion. Recenter and lower the right gripper toward the remaining white pen before closing.
Finish the empty left arm's near-origin return. The white pen is centered between the right jaws; descend a little and close, keeping the orientation fixed.
Settle the left arm at origin and test the white pen with a straight, slow lift. Keep the right gripper fully closed while assessing retention in RGB.
The white pen did not follow the lift. Reopen, shift along the shaft toward its middle rather than its tip, and approach a slightly deeper grasp.
Fine-correct the shaft's lateral offset and angle, lower about a centimeter, then close without lifting yet.
Make a slow vertical test lift with the right gripper closed, avoiding further downward contact with the table.
White pen remains between the jaws during lift. Carry it toward red with gentle yaw alignment and adequate rim clearance; keep the left arm at origin.
Bring the retained white pen fully over the red basket, keeping its shaft within the basket footprint before release.
Release the second white pen in red and allow it to settle. Withdraw toward the staged black pen, restoring a downward widthwise grasp orientation.
Approach the accessible right-hand portion of the staged black pen, staying on the right side of the centerline and keeping the empty left arm at origin.
Correct the black shaft's small sideways offset and angle from the wrist image, lower carefully and close on its right-hand section.
Allow the black-pen grip to close, then lift vertically without lateral or wrist motion to verify retention.
Black pen visibly followed the lift. Carry it toward red with the shaft horizontal and the gripper closed, keeping the whole pen clear of basket rims.
Continue the retained black pen toward red, positioning the cap near the basket's right side so the longer shaft also fits inside.
Lower the black pen fully into red, release it alongside the two white pens, and pause briefly for settling before returning the right arm.
All objects appear grouped in their baskets. Withdraw the empty right gripper upward and back, gradually restoring the home orientation while keeping elbow-up continuity.
Continue the right arm's smooth return toward origin with both grippers open. The baskets remain undisturbed and the pens are visibly settled in red.
Complete the right arm's decelerating return to its original pose, with both grippers open and the sorted objects left undisturbed.
